title: Mirage F1BE two-seater (DCS)

sources.title: DCS Mirage F1 Quick Start Guide (EN)

intro: The Mirage F1BE is the two-seat trainer of the Mirage F1. The front cockpit works like the F1CE and F1EE, with a selector unit added that hands the radar, the TACAN, the radio and the VOR/ILS between the seats. The instructor in the rear seat has a smaller panel with repeaters, a sight repeater screen and copies of the flight and engine controls.

areas.name: Left console
areas.text: The left side of the cockpit. In the F1BE it also holds the selector unit that hands systems over between the two seats.

panels.name: Selector unit (both cockpits)
panels.text: A small box of four lit pushbuttons and a test button that decides which seat controls the TACAN, the radar, the radio and the VOR/ILS.
panels.context: A selector unit sits in each cockpit. Pressing a button in one cockpit moves the control of that system to that cockpit. The unit is dimmed with the day/night switch or the panel lighting knob.

controls.name: TACAN priority pushbutton
controls.text: Pressing this lit pushbutton gives the cockpit it is in control of the TACAN unit. The light comes on to show that this cockpit now has control.
controls.context: To hand the TACAN unit over, the pushbutton in the other cockpit has to be pressed. The selector unit (commutation unit) in each cockpit lets either pilot take over a system. When the aircraft is powered, the front cockpit has priority.

controls.name: RADAR priority pushbutton
controls.text: Pressing this lit pushbutton gives the cockpit it is in control of the radar. The light comes on to show that this cockpit now has control.
controls.context: To hand the radar over, the pushbutton in the other cockpit has to be pressed. The selector unit (commutation unit) in each cockpit lets either pilot take over a system. When the aircraft is powered, the front cockpit has priority.

controls.name: V/UHF priority pushbutton
controls.text: Pressing this lit pushbutton gives the cockpit it is in control of the radio. The light comes on to show that this cockpit now has control. The UHF (red) radio panel is not installed in the rear cockpit, so that radio cannot be set from there, though the rear pilot can talk and listen on it through the intercom.
controls.context: To hand the radio over, the pushbutton in the other cockpit has to be pressed. The selector unit (commutation unit) in each cockpit lets either pilot take over a system. When the aircraft is powered, the front cockpit has priority.

controls.name: V/ILS priority pushbutton
controls.text: Pressing this lit pushbutton gives the cockpit it is in control of the VOR/ILS unit. The light comes on to show that this cockpit now has control.
controls.context: To hand the VOR/ILS unit over, the pushbutton in the other cockpit has to be pressed. The selector unit (commutation unit) in each cockpit lets either pilot take over a system. When the aircraft is powered, the front cockpit has priority.

controls.name: Commutation panel test button
controls.text: Pressing this button lights the lamps of the selector unit, to show that none is burnt out.
controls.context: There is one in each cockpit. It tests only the lamps of this box.

panels.name: Radios
panels.text: The two radios on the left console and the box that mixes their volume.
panels.context: The pilot talks with the push-to-talk button on the stick. The channels are stored radio frequencies that are set in the Mission Editor.

controls.name: MKR/BF/TP pushbutton/potentiometer (F1BE label)
controls.text: The game labels this knob 'MKR/BF/TP' on the F1BE radio selector unit, where the F1CE has 'RAP + CME'. As on the F1CE it is a pushbutton with a potentiometer, a knob that is pushed and turned.
controls.context: The manual describes only the F1CE version, the return button with the volume of the radar warning receiver. The F1BE function is not explained.

controls.name: TB/APP pushbutton/potentiometer (F1BE label)
controls.text: The game labels this knob 'TB/APP' on the F1BE radio selector unit, where the F1CE has 'MKR + TP'. As on the F1CE it is a pushbutton with a potentiometer.
controls.context: The manual describes only the F1CE version, which links to the ground crew by telephone. The F1BE function is not explained.

areas.name: Lower panel and pedestal
areas.text: The lower middle of the cockpit. In the F1BE the ejection seat has Mk 10 handles.

panels.name: Ejection seat
panels.text: The seat that fires the pilot out of the plane in an emergency, with its handles and safety pin.
panels.context: A pin keeps the seat from firing by accident while the plane is on the ground. It is removed before taxiing.

controls.name: Firing handle (Mk 10 seat)
controls.text: The handle that fires the front ejection seat. The F1BE has Martin-Baker Mk 10 seats instead of the ERM6 seats of the F1CE. The game names the control 'Firing handle'.
controls.context: There is no separate face blind handle on this front seat in the game.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: instrument panel
areas.text: The instructor's main panel in the rear seat. It has repeaters of the front cockpit and the copies of the controls the instructor may need.

panels.name: Rear cockpit main instrument panel
panels.text: The instructor's panel: a sight repeater screen, a camera and repeaters, plus copies of the most used instrument controls.
panels.context: Many items repeat what the front pilot sees or sets, so the instructor can follow and help during a flight.

controls.name: Sight repeater
controls.text: A small black-and-white TV screen that shows the instructor what the front pilot sees in his sight. A camera in the front cockpit records the sight, and the picture is reflected in a mirror toward the rear pilot.
controls.context: Its controls are on the sight repeater control panel next to it.

controls.name: Sight camera
controls.text: A film camera, mounted in the rear cockpit of the two-seater, that records the front cockpit's sight view. Recording starts when the front pilot pulls the gun trigger or presses the launch button.
controls.context: The manual says the camera is not implemented in this simulation. It has a test button, a retard knob, a cartridge eject button and a brightness switch.

controls.name: Armament master repeater indicator
controls.text: A light that copies the front cockpit's armament master switch. It is green when that switch is OFF and red when it is ON.
controls.context: It lets the instructor see at once whether the weapons are armed.

controls.name: Sight repeater control panel
controls.text: The small panel of the sight repeater with a brightness knob, a contrast knob, a color filter switch, a density filter switch and an ON-OFF switch. The five controls are listed in the panel 'Sight repeater control panel (rear)'.
controls.context: It controls only the instructor's picture, not the front pilot's sight.

controls.name: Fuselage indicators selected light
controls.text: A blue light that comes on when the front cockpit's feeder tank / fuselage selector switch is in the F position, which means the fuel gauges show the whole fuselage.
controls.context: The rear fuel gauge shows the same selection as the front one.

controls.name: Autopilot indicator repeater unit
controls.text: A small panel in the rear cockpit that repeats the lights of the front autopilot unit. It has a test button, the indicator lights and an intensity knob.
controls.context: The instructor can see what the autopilot is doing, but cannot switch it.

controls.name: Slaved altimeter pressure setting knob (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Turning this knob tells the altimeter the local air pressure so it reads the right height. A counter shows the setting in millibars.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The pilot sets it before take-off to the value the tower gives. The manual says the range is 930 to 1070 millibars.

controls.name: Reference airspeed knob (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Turning this knob moves a small marker around the speed dial. The pilot sets it to a speed to remember, for example the approach speed.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The marker is the reference speed index of the Mach/airspeed indicator.

controls.name: Emergency jettison button guard (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A hinged cover over the emergency jettison button. The pilot lifts the cover first, so the switch cannot be moved by accident, and closes it again afterwards.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The cover has its own clickable part in DCS. It belongs to the emergency jettison button; the real cockpit has a guard here as well.

controls.name: Emergency jettison button (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Pressing this button drops all the loads under the wings and the fuselage at once.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is for emergencies only. The wingtip missiles are not dropped by it; they have their own button.

controls.name: Afterburner lights INJ, ON and SRL (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Three lights about the afterburner, the extra fuel burned at the back of the engine. INJ shows that the afterburner fuel is being injected. ON (FON) shows that the afterburner burns. SRL (also called ADF) warns of a fault in the system that lets the throttle jump straight into afterburner.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. Pressing a light tests it. When the afterburner lights up, INJ goes out and ON comes on.

controls.name: Master failure warning light (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A double red and amber light. It lights when any lamp of the failure warning panel comes on. Pressing it switches it off and silences the horn; it is then ready for the next failure.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The lamp on the failure warning panel itself stays lit for as long as the fault is present.

controls.name: Spherical indicator pole setting / marker test knob (rear)

positions.name: P
positions.text: Pole: the ball tilts to its south pole.

controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Turning this knob to P tilts the ball so it rests at its south pole. Pressing it tests the marker light.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The marker light flashes when the plane flies over a marker beacon on the way to a runway.

controls.name: Landing gear, airbrake, nose wheel steering and combat flap lights (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Four lights in one group. The U/C light is about the landing gear. The airbrake light says the airbrake is out. The nose wheel steering light says the steering is completely off. The combat flaps light shows that the combat flaps are working.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The manual says a steady combat flaps light is normal inside the permitted speed range and a flashing one means the flaps are outside it. The lights can be pressed to test them.

controls.name: Spherical indicator day/night selector (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Changes the brightness of the marker light between day and night.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The marker light blinks when the plane passes a marker beacon.

controls.name: LIM light with horn (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A red light that comes on together with a warning horn when the plane goes beyond a permitted limit, for example too fast with the flaps, slats or landing gear out.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The horn tells the pilot to slow down or change the setting. Pressing the light tests it.

controls.name: BIP button (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. When the landing gear is down, pressing this button sends a short audio signal to the tower on the radio frequency in use. The pilot hears it too.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It tells the tower that the landing gear is down and locked. A test light shows the signal is being sent.

controls.name: Configuration indicator test button (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. This button tests the lights of the configuration indicator, the combat flaps light and the nose wheel steering light.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The pilot presses it to see that all these lights work.

controls.name: Fire warning light (engine / afterburner) with horn (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A red warning light with a horn. It lights when the engine or the afterburner is on fire.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. For an engine fire the manual says to cut the throttle and close the engine fuel cock at once; for an afterburner fire to cut the afterburner and close its fuel cock.

controls.name: MATRA 550 or Sidewinder jettison button (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Pressing this button starts the motors of the two missiles on the wingtips and releases them without arming them. They are launched, not dropped.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The wingtip missiles are not part of the normal jettison. The manual calls this the outer missile emergency launch button.

controls.name: MATRA 550 / Sidewinder jettison button guard (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A hinged cover over the outer missile emergency launch button. The pilot lifts the cover first, so the switch cannot be moved by accident, and closes it again afterwards.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The cover has its own clickable part in DCS. It belongs to the outer missile emergency launch button; the real cockpit has a guard here as well.

controls.name: Fuel transfer indicator test button (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Pressing this button lights the lights of the fuel transfer indicator, to check that they work.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is the test button for the fuel transfer indicator.

controls.name: Autopilot intensity control (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Turning this knob makes the lights of the autopilot buttons brighter or dimmer.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is one of the cockpit lighting controls.

controls.name: Autopilot unit test button (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Pressing this button lights all the lamps of the autopilot unit, so the pilot can see that none is burnt out.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It does not switch the autopilot on.

controls.name: Accelerometer reset button and rheostat (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Pressing this button clears the highest and lowest values the G-meter remembers. Turning the knob changes the instrument's lighting.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The pilot resets the memory before a flight.

controls.name: Standby horizon uncage and aircraft model control (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Pulling and turning this knob fully clockwise locks (cages) the horizon. Turning it back unlocks (uncages) it. Pulling it fast-levels the horizon. Turning it moves the model aircraft up or down.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The pilot uncages it during start-up and adjusts the model aircraft during taxiing.

controls.name: Additional target selector switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Chooses whether the next entry for the extra point is its bearing or its distance. It can be turned clockwise or counterclockwise.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is used together with the bearing/distance knob.

controls.name: Bearing/Distance selector knob (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Dials in the extra point: a direction in degrees or a distance in nautical miles from the beacon, depending on the other switch.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The values appear in the two windows of the indicator.

controls.name: Fuel quantity reset thumbwheel (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A small wheel that sets the fuel remaining counter back to the real fuel amount after refuelling.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. A DCS option can reset the counters automatically when the plane is rearmed and refuelled.

controls.name: Standby altimeter pressure setting knob (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Turning this knob sets the local air pressure on the standby altimeter, in the same way as the main one.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The pilot sets both altimeters before take-off.

controls.name: Scope erasing button (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Pressing this button wipes the screen to black.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. On the screen's label it is marked EFF.

controls.name: Storage adjustment (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. This knob sets how long the picture of an echo stays on the screen before it fades (the afterglow).
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. On the screen's label it is marked REM.

controls.name: Radar function selection (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A switch under the screen that selects special radar display functions, for example HA (high altitude), IC (short pulse) and V1 (a picture of the ground).
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The manual says these three functions are chosen with this selector.

controls.name: Scope intensity adjustment (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Turning this knob makes the picture on the radar screen brighter or darker.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. On the screen's label it is marked LUM.

controls.name: Radar test button (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Pressing this button starts a test run of the radar display.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The pilot uses it on the ground to see that the radar is healthy.

controls.name: Hydraulic pressure selector switch (rear)

positions.name: SDES-FS
positions.text: The gauge shows the ancillary and emergency brake pressure.

controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Chooses what the hydraulic gauge shows: the pressure of circuits 1 and 2, or the pressure of the emergency brake system.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The manual's cabin checks use '1 SERVOS 2'.

controls.name: Nose wheel steering high sensitivity button (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Decides how far the nose wheel turns for the same pedal movement: 45 degrees when pushed in (strong) and 7 degrees otherwise (gentle).
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The button pops out when there is no weight on the front wheel.

controls.name: Nose wheel steering switch guard (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A hinged cover over the nose wheel steering switch. The pilot lifts the cover first, so the switch cannot be moved by accident, and closes it again afterwards.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The cover has its own clickable part in DCS. It belongs to the nose wheel steering switch; the real cockpit has a guard here as well.

controls.name: Nose wheel steering switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Switches the steering of the front wheel off.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The cabin checks keep it on, under guard. The nose wheel steering light shows when the steering is completely off.

controls.name: Show/Hide Flight Stick (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. The game names this control 'Show/Hide Flight Stick'. It shows or hides the stick in the cockpit picture.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It does not change how the plane flies.

panels.name: Sight camera controls
panels.text: The controls of the film camera that records the front pilot's sight, mounted in the rear cockpit.
panels.context: The manual says the camera is not implemented in this simulation, but its controls are present in the cockpit.

controls.name: Recording camera day/night brightness switch
controls.text: Sets the brightness of the film remaining lights of the camera to day or night.
controls.context: It belongs to the camera's own indicator lights.

controls.name: Countdown timer and camera operation test button
controls.text: Pressing it tests the camera. The manual lists a test button on the camera.
controls.context: The camera does not work in the game.

controls.name: Recording camera retard knob
controls.text: Sets how long the camera keeps recording after the firing button is released (the overrun delay).
controls.context: The manual names this the retard selection knob.

controls.name: Recording camera eject button
controls.text: Pressing it ejects the film cartridge of the camera.
controls.context: The manual names it the cartridge ejection button.

panels.name: Sight repeater control panel (rear)
panels.text: The five controls of the black-and-white TV screen that repeats the front pilot's sight for the instructor.
panels.context: The controls change only the instructor's picture.

controls.name: Sight repeater brightness adjustment knob
controls.text: Turning this knob makes the picture on the repeater screen brighter or darker.
controls.context: It is the first of the five repeater controls.

controls.name: Sight repeater contrast adjustment knob
controls.text: Turning this knob changes the contrast of the picture on the repeater screen, the difference between its bright and dark parts.
controls.context: It works together with the brightness knob.

controls.name: Sight repeater density filter switch
controls.text: Switches a density filter in front of the picture on or off. A density filter darkens the picture.
controls.context: It is used when the picture is too bright.

controls.name: Sight repeater ON-OFF switch
controls.text: Switches the repeater screen on or off, like the power switch of a TV.
controls.context: It is the power switch of the repeater.

controls.name: Sight repeater color filter switch
controls.text: Switches a color filter in front of the picture on or off.
controls.context: A color filter can make the picture easier to read.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: left console
areas.text: The left side of the rear cockpit: the gear and brake handles, the engine switches, the radio, the radar handle and the priority switches.

panels.name: Rear cockpit left side panel
panels.text: The instructor's left console. It holds the priority switches that let the rear seat take over some systems, and copies of the engine, landing gear and radio controls.
panels.context: The landing gear, flaps, throttle and brake chute levers of both cockpits are mechanically linked, so moving one moves the other.

controls.name: High-lift devices priority switch guard
controls.text: A hinged cover over the high-lift devices priority switch. The pilot lifts the cover first, so the switch cannot be moved by accident, and closes it again afterwards. The manual says the switch returns to AV when the guard is closed.
controls.context: The cover has its own clickable part in DCS. It belongs to the high-lift devices priority switch; the real cockpit has a guard here as well.

controls.name: High-lift devices priority switch

positions.name: AR
positions.text: Rear: the combat flaps and slats are controlled from the rear cockpit only.

positions.name: AV
positions.text: Front: no control of auto-slats or combat flaps from the rear cockpit.

positions.name: RENT SEC
positions.text: Emergency retraction of flaps and slats.

controls.text: A guarded switch in the rear cockpit that decides who controls the combat slats and flaps: the rear pilot, the front pilot, or an emergency retraction.
controls.context: Only with the switch at AR can the rear pilot control the combat flaps and the automatic slats.

controls.name: Airbrake priority switch guard
controls.text: A hinged cover over the airbrake priority switch. The pilot lifts the cover first, so the switch cannot be moved by accident, and closes it again afterwards.
controls.context: The cover has its own clickable part in DCS. It belongs to the airbrake priority switch; the real cockpit has a guard here as well.

controls.name: Airbrake priority switch

positions.name: Forward
positions.text: Guard closed: any cockpit's airbrake switch can extend them, unless one is in the locked-out position.

positions.name: Aft
positions.text: Guard open: only the rear airbrake switch extends or retracts them.

controls.text: A guarded switch (labelled AF) that decides which airbrake switch has the last word. With the guard closed, either cockpit can extend the airbrakes. With the guard open and the switch aft, only the rear switch works.
controls.context: It lets the instructor take over the airbrakes from the front pilot.

controls.name: (C + M or SW) R deselection button (rear)
controls.text: A button in the rear cockpit that does the same as the front cockpit's deselection switch: it switches off the rapid cannon plus missile dogfight mode.
controls.context: It brings back the weapon choice made before the dogfight mode was used.

controls.name: Selector unit (rear)
controls.text: The rear cockpit's copy of the selector unit. It lets the rear pilot take over the TACAN, the radar, the radio and the VOR/ILS.
controls.context: Its buttons are listed in the panel 'Selector unit (both cockpits)'.

controls.name: Trim indicators (rear)
controls.text: Three small gauges in the rear cockpit that show how the roll, pitch and rudder trims are set.
controls.context: The rear stick has its own trim hat, so the instructor can see the effect on these gauges.

controls.name: Engine emergency regulation switch (rear cockpit)

positions.name: ARRET
positions.text: Emergency regulation is switched off in both cockpits.

controls.text: A guarded switch of the engine's emergency regulation in the rear cockpit. For the rear cockpit the manual describes an emergency regulation priority switch with three positions: rear, neutral and off.
controls.context: The game names this control 'Engine emergency regulation switch'. The manual's picture of the rear left panel shows the priority switch with its guard.

controls.name: MKR/BF/TP pushbutton/potentiometer (rear)
controls.text: The game labels this knob of the rear radio selector unit 'MKR/BF/TP'. Like the others it is a pushbutton with a potentiometer, a knob that is pushed and turned.
controls.context: The manual describes only the F1CE labels of the radio selector unit; the meaning of the label MKR/BF/TP is not explained.

controls.name: TB/APP pushbutton/potentiometer (rear)
controls.text: The game labels this knob of the rear radio selector unit 'TB/APP'. Like the others it is a pushbutton with a potentiometer.
controls.context: The manual describes only the F1CE labels of the radio selector unit; the meaning of the label TB/APP is not explained.

controls.name: MISS potentiometer (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Turning it sets the volume of the missile warning sound.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The missile warning comes from the radar warning system.

controls.name: U + V pushbutton/potentiometer (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Pressing it makes the V/UHF radio ready to transmit. Turning it changes the volume of that radio.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. Both knobs of the radio selector unit work by being pushed and turned.

controls.name: LP main cock switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. This is the main fuel tap of the engine and the afterburner (LP stands for low pressure). Closed, no fuel reaches the engine.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The cabin checks set it to closed and unguarded; for the start it is opened.

controls.name: LP main cock switch guard (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A hinged cover over the LP main cock switch. The pilot lifts the cover first, so the switch cannot be moved by accident, and closes it again afterwards.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The cover has its own clickable part in DCS. It belongs to the LP main cock switch; the real cockpit has a guard here as well.

controls.name: TAC potentiometer (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Turning it sets the volume of the TACAN radio signal.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. TACAN is a radio beacon that gives the direction and distance to it.

controls.name: VOR potentiometer (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Turning it sets the volume of the VOR radio signal.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. VOR is a radio beacon that gives the direction to it.

controls.name: U pushbutton/potentiometer (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Pressing it makes the UHF radio ready to transmit. Turning it changes the volume of that radio.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The V/UHF radio has its own knob next to it.

controls.name: AMPLI 2-1 selector switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Changes between two amplifiers in the box. Amplifier 1 is powered by the main DC bus and amplifier 2 by the battery bus.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. Channel 2 runs from the battery bus, so it does not depend on the main bus.

controls.name: Emergency regulation control lever (rear)

positions.name: Forward/Increase
positions.text: The engine speed increases in small steps.

positions.name: Aft/Decrease
positions.text: The engine speed decreases in small steps.

controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. In emergency regulation this lever takes the place of the throttle. It is moved in small steps, forward for more and aft for less engine speed.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. There is no rpm regulation in this mode, and the engine reacts slowly.

controls.name: Anti-skid (SPAD) switch guard (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A hinged cover over the anti-skid switch. The pilot lifts the cover first, so the switch cannot be moved by accident, and closes it again afterwards.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The cover has its own clickable part in DCS. It belongs to the anti-skid switch; the real cockpit has a guard here as well.

controls.name: Anti-skid (SPAD) switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Switches off the anti-skid system, which stops the wheels from locking up when braking, like the ABS of a car.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It stays on, under guard, in normal use.

controls.name: Throttle cut/idle switch (rear)

positions.name: Idle
positions.text: Forward: fuel on; used for the engine start.

controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A switch on the throttle that sets it to the idle position or to the stop position, where the engine gets no fuel.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The throttle must be at the stop before the engine start, and is moved to idle between 300 and 600 rpm.

controls.name: In-flight relight control (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Pressing this control tries to restart the engine in flight if it has gone out. It holds itself on for 30 seconds.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is hidden under the throttle. It needs the battery, so a flat battery stops the relight.

controls.name: Rudder trim control switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Trims the rudder by hand, that is, shifts the neutral position of the rudder so the plane flies straight without pushing the pedals.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It works when the anti-slip function is off. It is labelled TRIM DIRECT. in the cockpit.

controls.name: Slat/flap lever (rear)

positions.name: HOTAS flaps down
positions.text: Moves the lever toward more flaps.

positions.name: HOTAS flaps up
positions.text: Moves the lever toward less flaps.

controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. This lever sets the slats and flaps by hand for take-off and landing. The game calls its moves 'flaps down' and 'flaps up'.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It works together with the combat flap lever on the throttle and the selector switch next to it.

controls.name: Radar control stick scan selection (rear)

positions.name: Left
positions.text: A step of the scan width.

positions.name: Right
positions.text: A step of the scan width.

controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A switch at the front of the handle's base. It selects the width of the radar's side-to-side sweep, plus or minus 60 or plus or minus 30 degrees.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. A narrower sweep searches a smaller area faster.

controls.name: Radar control stick elevation/altitude difference button (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A button at the rear base of the radar handle. It chooses what the two handle buttons change: the antenna tilt (shown as E) or the altitude difference (shown as D).
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The letter appears on the radar screen's display.

controls.name: Radar control stick scale selection (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A switch at the rear of the handle's base. It selects the distance scale of the radar screen: 60, 35, 15 or 7 nautical miles.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The lit scale numbers on the screen show which one is chosen.

controls.name: A/B main cock switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. This is a fuel tap for the afterburner only. It can shut off the afterburner's fuel while the engine itself keeps running.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The cabin checks set it to ON and guarded. After an afterburner fire the pilot closes it.

controls.name: A/B main cock switch guard (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A hinged cover over the afterburner main cock switch. The pilot lifts the cover first, so the switch cannot be moved by accident, and closes it again afterwards.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The cover has its own clickable part in DCS. It belongs to the afterburner main cock switch; the real cockpit has a guard here as well.

controls.name: N-100%-EMG mode selector switch (rear)

positions.name: N
positions.text: Normal: a mixture of oxygen and air depending on height, and pure oxygen above 33,000 feet.
Pure oxygen on demand at any height.

positions.name: EMG
positions.text: Emergency: a steady flow of the mixture.

controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Chooses how the oxygen is supplied: normal, pure oxygen, or an emergency flow.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. A little blinker shows when oxygen is used on demand. A repeater shows N or a red square.

controls.name: Anti-G valve cock (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. The tap of the anti-G system, the suit that squeezes the legs in hard turns.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The manual only names it in a figure.

controls.name: Emergency/parking brake handle (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A handle that holds the brakes on when the plane is parked, or brakes the plane if the normal brakes do not work.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The cabin checks set the parking brake before engine start and release it before taxiing.

controls.name: Anti-retraction override button (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Normally the gear cannot be raised while the plane stands on the ground. Pressing this button allows it.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is a safety feature against raising the gear by mistake on the ground.

controls.name: Stick uncouple switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Frees the stick from the autopilot. If the autopilot is on, using this switch switches it off.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is labelled DEB. MANCHE (stick uncouple). It stays off, under guard, in normal flying.

controls.name: Undercarriage control lever (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. This lever moves the landing gear down or up. Pull it to extend or retract the wheels.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The pilot retracts the gear after take-off and extends it for landing. The safety lever beside it must be opened first.

controls.name: Stick uncouple switch guard (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A hinged cover over the stick uncouple switch. The pilot lifts the cover first, so the switch cannot be moved by accident, and closes it again afterwards.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The cover has its own clickable part in DCS. It belongs to the stick uncouple switch; the real cockpit has a guard here as well.

controls.name: Engine emergency regulation switch guard (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A hinged cover over the emergency regulation switch. The pilot lifts the cover first, so the switch cannot be moved by accident, and closes it again afterwards.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The cover has its own clickable part in DCS. It belongs to the emergency regulation switch; the real cockpit has a guard here as well.

controls.name: Emergency regulation light (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. This light comes on when the emergency regulation mode is switched on.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The pilot checks before line-up that it is out; before the first flight of the day a test of this mode is part of the procedure.

controls.name: V/UHF SIL (squelch) switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. SIL stands for silence. The switch turns on the squelch, which cuts the hiss of the radio when nobody talks.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is the same function as on a normal radio set.

controls.name: V/UHF test selector switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Starts a test of the radio's receiver or transmitter. It has a middle position for normal use.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. A test light shows that the transmitter test has started.

controls.name: V/UHF channel selector (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Chooses one of the 20 stored radio channels, like the station buttons of a car radio.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is used when the frequency mode switch is on P. A window shows the chosen number.

controls.name: V/UHF frequency thumbwheels (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Five small wheels for typing the frequency by hand: hundreds, tens, units, tenths and thousandths of megahertz.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. They are used when the frequency mode switch is on M.

controls.name: V/UHF frequency mode switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Chooses where the main frequency comes from: typed in by hand, a preset channel, or the guard frequency.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The marks are M (manual), P (preset) and G (guard).

controls.name: V/UHF 25W-5W switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Chooses the transmitter power, strong at 25 watts or weak at 5 watts.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. A weaker transmitter reaches less far.

controls.name: V/UHF function selector (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Switches the radio off or on and chooses whether it also listens to the guard channel.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The manual says AR is off, PAL uses only the main frequency, PAL+G also listens to the guard channel, and F1 and H are unused.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: right console
areas.text: The right side of the rear cockpit: the radio navigation boxes, the air conditioning, the lighting knobs and the armament repeaters.

panels.name: Rear cockpit right side panel
panels.text: The instructor's right console, with repeater lights for the armament, copies of the navigation boxes and the air conditioning controls.
panels.context: Here the instructor sees the weapon and radar choices of the front pilot and can set the TACAN, the VOR/ILS and the oxygen.

controls.name: Standby horizon and oxygen warning cut-off switches cover
controls.text: A spring-loaded cover over the standby horizon switch and the oxygen warning cut-off switch. It is used in solo flights to keep both switches off.
controls.context: When fully open it is held by a small piece shaped like a chess pawn, but only if both switches are off. Otherwise it springs shut.

controls.name: Oxygen warning cut-off switch
controls.text: Cancels the oxygen alarm of the rear cockpit. The alarm sounds when the rear pilot does not breathe through the mask for a few seconds.
controls.context: In solo flights, with nobody in the rear seat, the switch is set to cancel.

controls.name: Air conditioning master valve control switch guard
controls.text: A hinged cover over the rear master valve control switch. The pilot lifts the cover first, so the switch cannot be moved by accident, and closes it again afterwards.
controls.context: The cover has its own clickable part in DCS. It belongs to the rear master valve control switch; the real cockpit has a guard here as well.

controls.name: Auto/Manual selector switch guard
controls.text: A hinged cover over the rear auto/manual selector switch. The pilot lifts the cover first, so the switch cannot be moved by accident, and closes it again afterwards.
controls.context: The cover has its own clickable part in DCS. It belongs to the rear auto/manual selector switch; the real cockpit has a guard here as well.

controls.name: Auto/Manual selector switch
controls.text: The rear cockpit's own switch for automatic or manual control of the air conditioning. It sits under a guard.
controls.context: The manual describes the front version, which chooses automatic or manual control of the equipment temperature.

controls.name: Hot/Cold cabin selector switch
controls.text: The game names this control 'Hot/Cold cabin selector switch'. It works as a hot/cold selector for the rear cockpit's air conditioning.
controls.context: The manual describes only the front version, which acts on the equipment temperature.

controls.name: Demist switch guard
controls.text: A hinged cover over the rear demist switch. The pilot lifts the cover first, so the switch cannot be moved by accident, and closes it again afterwards.
controls.context: The cover has its own clickable part in DCS. It belongs to the rear demist switch; the real cockpit has a guard here as well.

controls.name: Warning horn switch guard
controls.text: A hinged cover over the rear warning horn switch. The pilot lifts the cover first, so the switch cannot be moved by accident, and closes it again afterwards.
controls.context: The cover has its own clickable part in DCS. It belongs to the rear warning horn switch; the real cockpit has a guard here as well.

controls.name: Armament repeater panel: radar selection lights
controls.text: Lights that show the radar mode the front pilot has chosen: off (ARRET), standby (VEIL) or transmit (EMISS).
controls.context: Their brightness follows the day/night switch or the panel lighting knob.

controls.name: Armament repeater panel: armament selection lights
controls.text: Lights that come on for the weapon mode the front pilot has chosen on the armament panel.
controls.context: They let the instructor follow the weapon choice. Each can be lit for test with the lights test button.

controls.name: AN/ALE-40 programmer (rear cockpit)
controls.text: In the two-seater the chaff and flare programmer sits on the right console of the rear cockpit. Its selectors set the number and spacing of the decoys.
controls.context: The seven selectors of the programmer are described with the single-seater's programmer behind the seat.

controls.name: VOR-ILS control unit (rear)
controls.text: The rear cockpit's box for tuning VOR and ILS radio beacons. It has an ON/OFF selector, a MHz selector, a kHz selector and a test selector.
controls.context: The VOR/ILS can be used by the seat that has the priority.

controls.name: TACAN control unit (rear)
controls.text: The rear cockpit's box for tuning the TACAN radio beacon system. It has a test button, an X/Y selector, a channel selector and a mode selector.
controls.context: The TACAN can be used by the seat that has the priority.

controls.name: VOR/TACAN mode repeater indicator
controls.text: A display that shows VOR or TAC to match the front cockpit's VOR-ILS/OFF/TACAN selector. It is white when that selector is off.
controls.context: It lets the instructor see which radio beacon feeds the front pilot's pointers.

controls.name: Oxygen indicator (rear)
controls.text: The rear cockpit's oxygen instrument, like the front one: a blinker, a quantity needle in quarters and a repeater of the selector position.
controls.context: A green band marks enough oxygen and a red band too little.

controls.name: Air conditioning control unit (rear)
controls.text: The rear cockpit's own air conditioning panel with its master valve switch, auto/manual switch, hot/cold switch and demist switch.
controls.context: Each switch of the unit is listed separately in this panel.

controls.name: Cannons too hot light (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A light that comes on when the cannons are too hot. Pressing it tests the light.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It sits on the right front panel.

controls.name: Standby horizon switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Switches the power of the standby horizon on and off.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The start-up list switches it on during the after-start checks.

controls.name: Failure warning panel O2 test button (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Pressing it tests the oxygen failure light and the oxygen warning sound.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The oxygen warning has its own sound that is different from the other warnings.

controls.name: Failure warning panel T test button (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Pressing it lights all the lamps of the failure warning panel and tests the master failure light and the warning sound for red lights.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is the general test of the warning system.

controls.name: Radar emergency transmission button (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Pressing it restarts the radar transmission or resets the radar power supply.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The manual calls it the SECOURS (emergency) pushbutton.

controls.name: Armament panel lights test (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Pressing it lights the lamps of the pushbuttons on this panel to prove they work.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is the test button for the panel.

controls.name: (C + M or SW) R light (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A green light that shows the dogfight mode is on, in which the guns and the wingtip missiles are armed together. The catalog also names the jammer detection light here.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The mode is switched on by the button on the throttle and off by a switch on the left wall.

controls.name: Oxygen test button (T button) (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Holding this button runs the oxygen quantity needle from empty to full. After release it should settle back at its start position.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. If the needle settles outside the green zone, the oxygen tank has to be changed.

controls.name: Air conditioning master valve control switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. The main switch of the cabin air system. It connects or disconnects the air conditioning and pressurization of the cabin and the cooling of the equipment bay.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The after-start list switches it on.

controls.name: Demist switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Forward, it lets warm air flow onto the front and left windows to clear mist.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The manual says the demist switch has no effect in DCS.

controls.name: Warning horn switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Switches the warning horn on. The horn sounds with the red lights of the failure warning panel and with other warnings.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The cabin checks require it ON; the test of the warning system uses it.

controls.name: Day/night selector switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. In the day position the indicator lights and panels are at full brightness and cannot be dimmed. In the night position they can be dimmed with the next knob.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. At night the maximum is slightly lower than by day.

controls.name: Light and panel lighting rheostat (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Adjusts the brightness of the indicator lights and panels, but only when the day/night switch is on night.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It also sets the brightness of the lit pushbuttons.

controls.name: Indicator lights brightness (EC) (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Sets the brightness of the status lights of the radar screen. The red fault lights are not affected.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. If a fault is present, these three red lights go out when the knob is at minimum.

controls.name: Strobe brightness (AL) (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Sets the brightness of the strobe, the bright line the pilot moves across the screen to choose a target.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The strobe is moved with the radar control stick.

controls.name: Distance markers brightness (MQ) (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Sets the brightness of the distance markers on the screen.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The markers help to read how far away an echo is.

controls.name: Horizon and radial velocity marker brightness (LH) (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Sets the brightness of the artificial horizon line and the radial speed marker on the screen.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The horizon line on the screen is moved up and down with the knob next to it.

controls.name: Horizon symbol vertical position (CH) (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Moves the artificial horizon line on the screen up or down.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is used together with the brightness knob for the horizon line.

controls.name: TACAN test button (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Starts a 10-second test. A green and a red lamp flash, then the green lamp must stay on.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. If the green stays off and the red lamp stays on, the TACAN is faulty.

controls.name: TACAN channel selectors (X/Y, hundreds-tens, units) (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Three knobs that set the TACAN channel: the X or Y mode, the hundreds and tens, and the units.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. Valid channels run from 01 to 116, X or Y. A window shows the channel.

controls.name: TACAN mode selector (rear)

positions.name: A/A
positions.text: Air to air: distance between two planes.

controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Chooses the TACAN mode: off, receive only, transmit and receive for direction and distance, or air to air.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. T/R is the normal mode for a direction and distance to a ground station.

controls.name: VOR/ILS ON/OFF selector (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Switches the VOR/ILS receiver on or off.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The after-start list switches it on.

controls.name: VOR/ILS MHz frequency selector (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Sets the whole-megahertz part of the VOR or ILS frequency.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is used together with the kHz selector.

controls.name: VOR/ILS test selector (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Starts a test of the VOR/ILS equipment. In the test positions a north bearing, or a maximum bar deviation, is shown.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The manual names the test positions HG and BD.

controls.name: VOR/ILS kHz frequency selector (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Sets the kilohertz part of the VOR or ILS frequency.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is used together with the MHz selector.

controls.name: Oxygen overpressure button (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. The game names it 'Oxygen overpressure button'. In this simulation it has no function.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The manual states that the overpressure button is not implemented in this simulation.

controls.name: Anti-G connection cover (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A cover on the connector for the anti-G suit hose. The anti-G suit squeezes the pilot's legs in hard turns.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The manual states that the cover is not implemented in this simulation.

controls.name: Anti-G test button (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A button to test the anti-G system of the pilot's suit.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The manual only names it in a figure; it does not describe the test.

controls.name: Ultraviolet lighting rheostat (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Adjusts the ultraviolet light that makes the markings of the main panel instruments glow.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is turned up only when the cockpit is dark.

controls.name: Dual instrument panel lighting rheostat (floodlights) (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. The outer knob of a double knob. It sets the brightness of the red floodlights on the instrument panel.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The inner knob of the same pair sets the integral lights.

controls.name: Dual instrument panel lighting rheostat (integral) (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. The inner knob of a double knob. It sets the brightness of the red lights built into the instrument panel.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The outer knob sets the floodlights.

controls.name: Dual console and pedestal lighting rheostat (floodlights) (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. The outer knob of a second double knob. It sets the brightness of the red floodlights on the consoles and the pedestal.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The inner knob sets their integral lights.

controls.name: Dual console and pedestal lighting rheostat (integral) (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. The inner knob of the second double knob. It sets the brightness of the red lights built into the consoles and the pedestal.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The outer knob sets the floodlights.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: seat, canopy and clock
areas.text: The rear seat's canopy handles, mirrors, clock, lamp knobs, brake chute control and ejection handles.

panels.name: Rear cockpit canopy, clock and seat
panels.text: The controls around the rear seat: the canopy handles, the mirrors, the clock, the brake chute control and the ejection handles.
panels.context: They are the rear twins of the front cockpit's canopy, clock and ejection controls.

controls.name: Firing handle (rear seat)
controls.text: The handle that fires the rear ejection seat. The F1BE has Martin-Baker Mk 10 seats in both cockpits. The game names the control 'Firing handle'.
controls.context: The ERM6 seats of the single-seater are replaced by Mk 10 seats in the two-seater, as the annex of the manual says.

controls.name: Canopy hinged handle (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A hinged handle that keeps the canopy open a little, like the stay that holds a window ajar.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The start-up list of the manual allows the engine to be started with the canopy closed or partly open.

controls.name: Clock winding/setting lever (rear)

positions.name: PUSHED
positions.text: Turning the knob winds the clock spring.

positions.name: PULLED
positions.text: Turning the knob sets the time.

controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A small lever that decides what turning the clock knob does. Pushed in, the knob winds the clock. Pulled out, the knob sets the time.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is used together with the chronometer and winding knob.

controls.name: Miscellaneous instrument integral lighting rheostat (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. This knob sets the brightness of the built-in lighting of the standby compass, the clock and the accelerometer (the G-meter).
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is one of several dimmers in the cockpit lighting group; the others sit on the right console.

controls.name: Miscellaneous instrument lighting switch (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A switch of the lighting group. The manual lists it together with the lighting of the angle-of-attack indicator tape, the scale strip of that instrument.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The manual does not describe its positions further; the game names it 'Miscellaneous instrument lighting switch'.

controls.name: Map light rheostat (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. This knob makes the map light brighter or dimmer. The map light is a small lamp for reading a paper map.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It belongs to the cockpit lighting group that the manual describes with the lighting control unit.

controls.name: Chronometer start / clock winding knob (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Pushing this knob starts, stops and resets the stopwatch. Turning it clockwise winds the clock. With the setting lever pulled, turning it sets the time.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It works together with the winding/setting lever next to it. Together they keep the clock wound and set.

controls.name: Incidence indicator lighting rheostat (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Turning this knob changes the brightness of the angle-of-attack lights.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It sets the coloured lights independently of the other instrument lights.

controls.name: Canopy lock control (rear)

positions.name: AFT
positions.text: The canopy is unlocked and can be opened.

controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. This lever locks the closed canopy to its frame so it cannot blow open in flight. Forward locks it, aft frees it.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The pilot moves it forward when the canopy is fully closed during start-up and checks that the P.CAB light is out before lining up for take-off.

controls.name: Trim hat (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A small four-way switch on top of the grip for the thumb. It trims the plane: up and down for the pitch trim, left and right for the roll trim.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. While the autopilot is on, the same hat gives short pulses that change the held pitch and heading (BIP trim): a pitch pulse changes the attitude by 0.8 degrees and a roll pulse the heading by 2 degrees.

controls.name: Rear-view mirror (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. The game calls this control 'Adjust/Hide Mirror (rotate or click)'. Turning it aims the mirror; clicking it hides the mirror or shows it again.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. One mirror sits on each side. The game gives the fold and unfold actions their own commands, so they can be put on a key or button.

controls.name: Canopy open/close handles (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Two handles on the left and right of the canopy frame. The pilot grabs them to push the canopy open or to pull it shut by hand.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The canopy is moved by hand, not by a motor. In DCS it can also be opened and closed with a key command.

controls.name: Brake chute control (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A handle for the brake parachute under the tail. Pulling it aft opens the chute; pushing it forward drops it.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It can be used only on the ground, up to 210 knots. The cabin checks require it forward.

controls.name: Canopy embrittle control (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A handle for emergencies. Pulling it sets off a small charge that makes the canopy glass crack, so it breaks away easily when the pilot has to leave the plane.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. The ejection seat sets off the same system by itself. In normal flying the handle stays aft, as the cabin checks require.

controls.name: Ejection handle safety pin (rear)

positions.name: INSTALL
positions.text: The pin is in: the seat is safe.

positions.name: REMOVE
positions.text: The pin is out: the seat is ready to fire.

controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. A pin that blocks the ejection handle so the seat cannot fire by accident on the ground.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is removed before taxiing and put back after parking.

controls.name: Seat height adjustment control (rear)
controls.text: This is the rear-seat copy of a front control. Moves the seat up or down so the pilot sits at the right height.
controls.context: Rear cockpit copy. It is part of getting into the cockpit; the manual lists it with the entry checks.
